subject: Development inventory
study: Compiler versus interpreter; source, executable, host and target
implementation: Create a learning repository; record phone model, real RAM, Android version, available storage, computer compiler and Python versions; compile a hello-world C++ program
acceptance: Run the executable from a terminal and explain every command; distinguish physical RAM from RAM expansion

subject: Variables and initialization
study: Basic types, initialization, cout, cin, statements and compiler diagnostics
implementation: Write a CLI that asks for parameter count and bit width and estimates raw weight bytes; use double for the first version
acceptance: Check 1B at 4 bits gives 500 million decimal bytes; distinguish GB from GiB; reject a negative input

subject: Functions and parameters
study: Return types, local scope, pass by value and function declarations
implementation: Split the estimator into conversion, estimation and presentation functions; add KV and runtime allowance as explicit user inputs
acceptance: Explain why the result is an estimate rather than phone capacity; manually check three configurations

subject: Phone development connection
study: ADB, developer options, host-target separation; upstream Android build guide
implementation: Enable debugging, connect by USB, inspect device properties and run a harmless shell command; choose one small model and record its origin and terms
acceptance: Save device metadata and the exact model identity; do not claim an accelerator works before a model runs

subject: First native baseline
study: Runtime commit, release build, model hash, CPU execution and context limits
implementation: Follow upstream instructions for the pinned checkout; deploy a CPU executable and run one short prompt; save the complete command and logs
acceptance: Confirm generation occurs on the phone and backend logs identify CPU; record actual tokens rather than word counts

subject: Simple Python experiment runner
study: subprocess argument lists, timeouts, JSON records and error capture
implementation: Write an ADB wrapper for one inference run; capture stdout, stderr, return code, elapsed time and configuration
acceptance: Disconnect the device or use a bad path and confirm a structured failure record; do not hide errors

subject: Week-one reconstruction
study: Recall variables, functions and the host-target build path
implementation: Rewrite the weight estimator without notes; reproduce one phone run; write a one-page explanation of what you measured
acceptance: A fresh shell can reproduce your command; list three unknowns and choose one to resolve next week

subject: Conditions and validation
study: if, else, booleans, comparison, short-circuit evaluation
implementation: Add model-size and quantization validation to the estimator; separate validation from output
acceptance: Zero, negative, absurdly large and malformed input receive deliberate behavior; explain each branch

subject: Loops and running statistics
study: for and while loops; counters and accumulation
implementation: Write a C++ latency-summary program over a fixed array; calculate count, min, max and arithmetic mean
acceptance: Check an empty list and a single value; compare against Python and explain why an average hides outliers

subject: Floating-point behavior
study: Float versus double, rounding, relative and absolute error
implementation: Create cancellation and summation examples; implement a numeric comparison helper
acceptance: Demonstrate why exact equality fails for some calculations; use a scale-aware tolerance with a near-zero case

subject: Integers and size arithmetic
study: Fixed-width integers, size_t, signedness and checked multiplication
implementation: Rework byte-size estimation with checked integer operations; retain a separate display conversion
acceptance: Oversized dimensions fail before wraparound; explain why casting after overflow cannot repair it

subject: Strings and configuration
study: std::string, parsing and error states; avoid dangling views for now
implementation: Parse a simple command line for model label, context and threads; keep options few and documented
acceptance: Unknown flags and missing values fail clearly; quoted paths are handled by the calling shell or argument list

subject: Small baseline matrix
study: Prefill versus decode, thread counts, fresh versus reused process
implementation: Extend the Python runner to three prompt lengths and two thread counts with three repetitions each
acceptance: Keep actual input/output counts; report individual observations plus median; do not equate fresh process with cold filesystem cache

subject: Review and measurement audit
study: Distinguish load, tokenization, queueing, prefill and first-token display
implementation: Draw the timing boundaries in prose; rewrite one function from memory and inspect every baseline log
acceptance: Identify one confound such as charging or prompt-template variation; correct the next experiment plan

subject: References and const
study: Object identity, aliases, const references and parameter contracts
implementation: Implement vector sum and normalization with explicit input/output ownership; compare pass-by-value and const-reference signatures
acceptance: Predict which calls copy data; explain why const is an interface property and not a thread-safety guarantee

subject: Pointers and lifetimes
study: Addresses, dereference, null, object lifetime and storage duration
implementation: Write tiny safe pointer examples; deliberately inspect a dangling pointer example in an isolated failing test
acceptance: Explain precisely when the pointee dies; do not run known undefined behavior in normal application code

subject: std::vector
study: Size, capacity, contiguous storage and iterator invalidation
implementation: Build a vector-based dot product with dimension validation; inspect capacity changes during append
acceptance: Test mismatched sizes and zero length; explain why reallocation can invalidate pointers and references

subject: std::array and spans
study: Fixed extent versus dynamic containers; non-owning std::span
implementation: Implement dot-product and min/max functions taking spans so array and vector callers share code
acceptance: Both owners can call the same function; document that a span does not extend the underlying lifetime

subject: Debugger workflow
study: Breakpoints, step into/over, stack frames and variable inspection
implementation: Introduce an indexing bug in a small program and find it with GDB or LLDB before reading the answer
acceptance: Save a short debugging transcript showing the first wrong state, not merely the final crash

subject: Sanitizer workflow
study: AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer; debug symbols
implementation: Build isolated out-of-bounds and use-after-free tests; repair them and add regression cases
acceptance: The tools diagnose the intentional failures where supported; repaired normal tests run clean; keep unsafe demos separate

subject: Closed-book container challenge
study: Pointers, spans, lifetime, resizing and const
implementation: Implement cosine similarity from an empty file with explicit zero-vector behavior; review all borrowed views
acceptance: Match a Python oracle and explain every container choice; name the lifetime assumptions in the API

subject: Structs and invariants
study: Members, aggregate initialization, encapsulation and class invariants
implementation: Create a Shape type with checked element count and a documented policy on zero dimensions
acceptance: Invalid shapes cannot silently allocate a wrapped size; unit tests cover rank and zero policy

subject: Constructors and RAII
study: Initialization lists, destructors, resource acquisition and cleanup
implementation: Create an owning FP32 Tensor using vector storage and Shape; provide checked indexing
acceptance: Construction establishes a valid state; throwing validation does not leak resources

subject: Copy and move semantics
study: Value semantics, references, move operations and moved-from states
implementation: Instrument a small demonstration type; compare copying Tensor with moving it; prefer the rule of zero where possible
acceptance: Predict the observed operations before running; explain why std::move does not itself move bytes

subject: Smart pointers
study: unique_ptr, shared_ptr, ownership graphs and cycles
implementation: Wrap a small opaque resource in unique ownership; design session and model ownership on paper
acceptance: No shared_ptr is added without a shared-ownership reason; destruction order is testable

subject: Views and reshaping
study: Owning tensors versus borrowed views; contiguity and shape compatibility
implementation: Implement TensorView over a span and reshape for contiguous tensors; document invalidation
acceptance: Reject mismatched element counts; test views while the owner is stable and demonstrate the invalidation hazard separately

subject: Enums and errors
study: enum class, error categories, exceptions and alternative return values
implementation: Define shape, dtype and load errors; make CLI boundaries convert failures into readable diagnostics
acceptance: A malformed operation reports the right category; no catch-all silently converts a failure into a valid tensor

subject: Tensor design review
study: Invariants, rule of zero, copies, borrows and failure paths
implementation: Write a short API document and simplify your implementation; reconstruct TensorView without reference
acceptance: Explain who owns each byte and when each view becomes invalid; all tensor tests pass

subject: CMake targets
study: Source lists, libraries, executables, include paths and target-scoped settings
implementation: Create a core library, CLI and test target; set your own code to C++20 without changing upstream requirements
acceptance: A clean out-of-tree debug build and release build both work; document exact commands

subject: Testing fundamentals
study: Fixtures, assertions, boundary cases and independent expected results
implementation: Use a lightweight test framework or CTest executable; test shapes, dot products, reshape and parsing
acceptance: At least one intentionally broken implementation fails a meaningful test; tests are not copies of the implementation

subject: Algorithms and lambdas
study: Iterators, range algorithms, captures and comparator contracts
implementation: Replace appropriate manual loops with standard algorithms; implement a deterministic top-k reference
acceptance: Tied values have documented behavior; explain any reference captured by a stored lambda

subject: Templates in moderation
study: Function templates, type deduction and compile-time constraints
implementation: Generalize one small utility for float and double; compare with an ordinary overload
acceptance: Both instantiations are tested; remove abstraction if it obscures ownership or error behavior

subject: Binary checkpoint specification
study: Byte order, magic, version, dtype, dimensions, offsets and lengths
implementation: Write a format specification before code; export two tensors from Python with explicit endian encoding
acceptance: A hand-inspected byte layout matches the spec; never serialize a compiler-dependent C++ struct directly

subject: Defensive checkpoint reader
study: Stream I/O, file size, checked offsets and validation before allocation
implementation: Read the tiny format in C++; reject invalid magic, unsupported version, truncation and inconsistent tensor sizes
acceptance: Generate separate corrupted fixtures; each fails before an unsafe read or unreasonable allocation

subject: Clean-build checkpoint drill
study: Reproducible builds and cross-language agreement
implementation: Build from a clean directory and load Python-exported tensors; compare every value and shape
acceptance: A peer could reproduce using only your README; capture compiler and dependency versions

subject: Threads and races
study: Thread lifetime, join, shared state and data races
implementation: Write a two-thread counter example and a corrected version; keep the broken version in a separate test area
acceptance: Explain why apparent correct output does not prove race freedom; use ThreadSanitizer on a supported host build

subject: Mutexes and condition variables
study: Lock ownership, predicate waits, spurious wakeups and shutdown
implementation: Implement a bounded producer-consumer queue with a mutex and condition variables
acceptance: Empty waits, full waits and shutdown all terminate; test a waiting producer and consumer

subject: Cancellation semantics
study: Cooperative cancellation, request state and terminal events
implementation: Add request IDs and cancellation to a one-worker job executor; define queued versus running cancellation
acceptance: Each request emits exactly one terminal result; cancellation checks occur at documented safe points

subject: Python-to-C++ boundary
study: Bindings, array ownership, contiguous buffers and GIL concepts
implementation: Expose your dot product or Tensor operation using pybind11; reject unsupported dtype/layout rather than silently misreading it
acceptance: Noncontiguous input is rejected or explicitly copied; input owner stays alive during native access

subject: Memory mapping and page faults
study: Virtual addresses, resident pages, mmap, copy-on-write and file-backed storage
implementation: Add an optional read-only mapped checkpoint loader on your host; keep the stream loader for comparison
acceptance: Understand that mapped file size is not resident memory; validate offsets before producing views

subject: Parallel work and false sharing
study: Partitioned output, reductions, synchronization and cache lines
implementation: Parallelize independent rows of a matrix-vector operation with a simple fixed partition
acceptance: Matches single-thread output within tolerance; measure enough work to expose overhead and report a slower small case

subject: Foundation gate
study: Ownership, threads, binary validation and build reproducibility
implementation: Review your queue under stress and draw the ownership of model, session and temporary buffers
acceptance: No unsupported claim of production readiness; list unresolved races, lifetime risks and portability limits explicitly

subject: Tensor layout and linear algebra
study: Batch, sequence, hidden size, strides and matrix orientation
implementation: Write explicit-shape NumPy or PyTorch examples for linear projection and batched matmul
acceptance: Annotate every dimension and compare one tiny multiplication against a hand calculation

subject: Stable softmax
study: Exponent overflow, max subtraction, axis selection and masking
implementation: Implement stable softmax and causal masking without calling the high-level attention API
acceptance: Rows normalize correctly; large logits remain finite; define behavior for an all-masked row

subject: Normalization
study: RMSNorm versus LayerNorm; epsilon and reduction precision
implementation: Implement RMSNorm with explicit dtype handling and compare to a trusted reference
acceptance: Test zero, constant and high-magnitude inputs; choose a numeric tolerance justified by dtype

subject: Rotary positions
study: Pair rotation, positions, frequencies and architecture conventions
implementation: Implement RoPE for a tiny tensor; isolate configuration and layout conventions
acceptance: Position zero behaves as expected; pair norms are preserved within rounding error; compare exact convention to the checkpoint

subject: Attention reference
study: Q, K, V, causal scores, scaling and head dimensions
implementation: Implement ordinary multi-head causal attention with explicit tensor operations
acceptance: Changing a future token cannot affect earlier outputs; a small example matches a manual or trusted computation

subject: Feed-forward and residuals
study: SwiGLU, activation, gated projections and residual stream
implementation: Implement one compatible decoder block from your chosen architecture, including both residual paths
acceptance: Validate intermediate shapes and outputs; do not substitute architecture details without documenting them

subject: Math reconstruction
study: Forward-pass dependencies and numeric stability
implementation: Rebuild the block from a blank file, then compare it with the previous version
acceptance: Explain every matmul and reduction; save deterministic reference tensors for later C++ tests

subject: Architecture contract
study: Config fields, tied embeddings, attention variants and checkpoint keys
implementation: Select one small supported checkpoint; map each tensor name and shape to your reference architecture
acceptance: Stop and resolve any mismatch rather than coercing shapes; record model revision and config

subject: Checkpoint loading
study: State dictionaries, dtype conversion and inference mode
implementation: Load weights into the Python reference; compare the first block against the official implementation
acceptance: Use a fixed token-ID sequence and compare named intermediates; isolate the first layer that diverges

subject: Full forward parity
study: Final norm, output head and vocabulary logits
implementation: Run the full model for a short token sequence and compare logits
acceptance: Report max absolute error and selected logits; explain why argmax alone is insufficient validation

subject: Tokenizer and chat template
study: BPE or model-specific tokenization, special tokens, BOS/EOS and templates
implementation: Use the official tokenizer; create fixed text-to-token fixtures including Unicode and whitespace
acceptance: Round trips and special-token behavior are documented; distinguish instruction template changes from model changes

subject: KV cache implementation
study: Prefill, per-layer K/V storage, cache positions and context bounds
implementation: Add cache updates and one-token decode to your Python reference
acceptance: Cached and uncached logits agree for the same prefix within tolerance; reset actually clears session state

subject: Sampling and sequence limits
study: Greedy, temperature, seeded randomness, stop rules and logits processing
implementation: Implement greedy and basic temperature sampling; bound total context and generated tokens
acceptance: EOS and limit termination work; fixed-seed tests are reproducible within the controlled implementation

subject: Reference freeze
study: Model identity, fixtures and deterministic debug workloads
implementation: Freeze a small golden fixture set for operations, one block and full cached decode
acceptance: Write the exact numeric comparison contract; keep large weights out of your source repository

subject: Matrix-vector kernel
study: Row-major layout, indexing and accumulation precision
implementation: Implement FP32 matvec against your TensorView; export random and adversarial fixtures from Python
acceptance: Test non-square shapes and mismatched dimensions; compare absolute and relative error

subject: RMSNorm in C++
study: Reduction, epsilon and output buffering
implementation: Port the Python RMSNorm with preallocated output and no hidden shape assumptions
acceptance: Match fixtures including zeros and extremes; document in-place aliasing support or reject aliasing

subject: RoPE in C++
study: Position indexing, frequency storage and rotation convention
implementation: Port the chosen model's RoPE; precompute only what the configuration requires
acceptance: Match Python across multiple positions; include a test that catches the wrong dimension pairing

subject: Softmax and attention
study: Stable exponentiation, causal bounds and score buffers
implementation: Implement scalar attention for one head then multiple heads; use explicit strides
acceptance: Match small reference tensors; verify future-token masking and finite outputs

subject: Feed-forward and decoder block
study: Intermediate buffers, activation and residual update order
implementation: Assemble one decoder block using your tested kernels
acceptance: Compare every stage with Python rather than debugging only final output; report first divergence

subject: Checkpoint-to-native bridge
study: Exported tensor names, config and endian-safe loading
implementation: Extend your educational format for the selected tiny checkpoint and load one complete block
acceptance: All shapes and lengths validated; no silent transpose; reject an unsupported architecture field

subject: Block parity gate
study: Numerical debugging and code review
implementation: Run all block fixtures, fix the earliest divergence and explain any tolerance change
acceptance: Do not move to full generation until block parity is established; list any model-specific assumptions

subject: Whole-model execution
study: Layer iteration, embedding lookup, final norm and output projection
implementation: Assemble the complete forward pass for token IDs using your validated blocks
acceptance: Compare final logits for a short fixed sequence; invalid token IDs fail cleanly

subject: Native KV cache
study: Layout, current position, capacity and session ownership
implementation: Implement fixed-capacity cache allocation and append; separate immutable model weights from mutable session state
acceptance: Two sessions do not share cache contents; boundary and reset cases match Python

subject: Prefill and decode paths
study: Full prefix versus incremental step and reusable workspace
implementation: Implement prefill and one-token decode functions with clearly timed boundaries
acceptance: Cache and uncached paths agree; avoid per-token workspace growth

subject: Streaming and cancellation
study: Token events, completion events and cooperative stop checks
implementation: Expose a token callback and cancellation flag in the CLI; define callback thread and lifetime
acceptance: Exactly one terminal status follows completion or cancellation; callbacks cannot outlive their session

subject: Tokenizer integration
study: External token IDs first, compatible tokenizer second
implementation: Keep a token-ID debug mode and integrate a trusted tokenizer interface; preserve template fixtures
acceptance: End-to-end text prompt produces the same input IDs as the reference; Unicode output is not split into invalid UI fragments

subject: Reference implementation reading
study: Small C inference code versus your C++ structure
implementation: Read selected llama2.c forward and generation code after writing your own; note five design differences
acceptance: Explain correctness or ownership implications; do not paste an implementation you cannot reconstruct

subject: Engine milestone
study: Parity, bounds, errors and reproducibility
implementation: Run a clean end-to-end generation demo and write an architecture note with model/session/workspace ownership
acceptance: The tiny model works on host; report supported architecture and limitations rather than claiming general GGUF compatibility

subject: Benchmark validity
study: Warmup, repetition, clocks, optimizer elimination and work accounting
implementation: Build a kernel benchmark with checksummed output and multiple input sizes
acceptance: Release builds do useful work; record raw observations and separate setup from the timed region

subject: Profile before changing code
study: Sampling versus instrumentation, symbols and call stacks
implementation: Profile host decode and annotate time in matvec, attention, allocation and other work
acceptance: Choose the largest actionable bottleneck using evidence; save a baseline profile

subject: Allocation discipline
study: Capacity reuse, arenas as a concept and lifetime-bound workspaces
implementation: Count or instrument allocations during decode; preallocate one repeated temporary buffer
acceptance: Correctness remains unchanged; report allocation count and latency before and after

subject: Cache locality
study: Contiguous traversal, strides and working-set size
implementation: Compare row and column traversal on matrices that fit and exceed cache
acceptance: Explain observed differences without attributing every result to bandwidth; repeat to check noise

subject: Bandwidth and arithmetic intensity
study: Bytes moved, FLOPs, roofline estimates and batch-one decode
implementation: Estimate weight bytes read per token and achievable bandwidth; compare with measured decode
acceptance: State assumptions and explain why the simple bound is not a hardware guarantee

subject: Prefill versus decode workload
study: Matrix-matrix versus matrix-vector shapes; amortization
implementation: Benchmark several prompt lengths and output lengths separately
acceptance: Show that one tokens-per-second number cannot describe both phases; include context length in decode results

subject: Optimization proposal
study: Amdahl's law, confounds and experiment scope
implementation: Write three optimization hypotheses ranked by impact and effort; implement only the smallest justified change
acceptance: A report includes unchanged correctness tests and a confidence-limited interpretation of the measurements

subject: Quantization arithmetic
study: Scale, zero point, signed ranges, clipping and rounding
implementation: Implement scalar symmetric quantize/dequantize in Python with an explicit representable range
acceptance: Zero, boundaries, ties and outliers have specified behavior; test round-trip error

subject: Granularity
study: Per-tensor, per-output-channel and group scales
implementation: Quantize one linear layer at each granularity and report error by output channel
acceptance: Scale indexing is tested; compare storage including scale overhead rather than raw integer data only

subject: Native integer representation
study: Weight storage, accumulator width and overflow bounds
implementation: Write an INT8 loader and reference quantized matvec; keep the activation path explicitly documented
acceptance: Compare against dequantized reference; explain whether your first kernel uses integer or floating-point multiplication

subject: Calibration
study: Representative input distribution and activation ranges
implementation: Collect layer statistics on a small public corpus; compare calibration sets from two domains
acceptance: No evaluation examples leak into tuning; report saturation and outlier effects

subject: End-to-end quantized model
study: Mixed precision, sensitive layers and integration
implementation: Replace selected projections with quantized versions; keep a float reference switch
acceptance: Layer and model numeric comparisons pass the chosen quality contract; quantify memory and latency

subject: Task evaluation
study: Perplexity as one signal; application-level quality and failure cases
implementation: Create a fixed text evaluation subset and report float versus INT8 outcomes
acceptance: Keep tokenizer, prompts and decoding fixed; manually inspect examples where behavior changes

subject: Quantization report
study: Compression, performance and quality tradeoffs
implementation: Write a result table including scale overhead, artifact size, memory and task scores
acceptance: If INT8 is slower, explain likely unpacking or kernel overhead and retain the honest result

subject: Bit operations
study: Masks, shifts, sign extension and integer promotions
implementation: Implement encode/decode for signed 4-bit values; document your nibble ordering
acceptance: Exhaustively round-trip all representable values and both nibble positions; do not rely on ambiguous signed shifts

subject: Packing arrays
study: Odd lengths, padding and byte counts
implementation: Pack arbitrary-length arrays and record the original element count
acceptance: Lengths 0, 1, 2, 3 and large odd arrays pass; unused bits cannot produce a phantom value

subject: Group quantization
study: Group boundaries, scale storage and tail groups
implementation: Implement grouped INT4 export in Python and decode in C++
acceptance: Check dimensions not divisible by group size; include scale metadata in the file size

subject: Reference INT4 matvec
study: Unpack, rescale and accumulate without changing the model contract
implementation: Implement an intentionally simple correctness-first kernel
acceptance: Matches Python dequantized computation; document where quantization error enters

subject: Fused dequantization
study: Temporary buffers, repeated unpacking and data reuse
implementation: Compare pre-dequantized, per-call dequantized and inner-loop unpacking approaches
acceptance: Measure separately on small and large matrices; include temporary memory and setup time

subject: Model experiment
study: Sensitivity, group size and mixed precision choices
implementation: Run a small sweep of two group sizes and selected quantized layers
acceptance: Use the frozen task set and identical generation settings; do not optimize only perplexity

subject: Quantization gate
study: Compatibility versus educational formats
implementation: Write a precise format description and compare concepts with runtime-supported quants
acceptance: State that your INT4 format is educational and not automatically GGUF, QNN or hardware-native INT4

subject: Vectorization fundamentals
study: SIMD lanes, loads, reductions, alignment and tails
implementation: Inspect compiler vectorization for your scalar dot product on the target
acceptance: Save compiler diagnostics or assembly; identify vector and scalar remainder paths

subject: First NEON kernel
study: ARM intrinsics for vector multiply-add and reduction
implementation: Implement one FP32 dot-product kernel with a scalar fallback
acceptance: Test odd lengths, tiny lengths and unaligned starting offsets where allowed; compare numerical error

subject: Quantized kernel experiment
study: Packed data, unpack cost and accumulation
implementation: Optimize one INT8 or INT4 inner loop only after the reference passes
acceptance: Compare output and throughput across representative shapes; keep unsupported instruction paths disabled

subject: Thread count and partitioning
study: Work size, scheduling overhead and heterogeneous cores
implementation: Sweep a few thread counts with fixed workloads and supported affinity experiments if available
acceptance: Do not assume all cores maximize performance; report sustained results and permitted controls

subject: False sharing and buffers
study: Cache-line sharing, independent output and synchronization
implementation: Construct a controlled false-sharing example, then revise data placement
acceptance: Explain why the demonstration may vary with hardware; never treat padding as a universal optimization

subject: Fusion or reuse experiment
study: Removing a temporary or repeated computation
implementation: Try one small fusion or workspace reuse based on profiling; retain reference operation tests
acceptance: Measure total decode impact, not just an isolated hot-loop speedup

subject: Optimization milestone
study: Performance claims and reproducible evidence
implementation: Publish a local report with one successful optimization and one failed hypothesis
acceptance: Every claimed improvement includes workload, build, repetitions and correctness evidence

subject: Cross-compilation fundamentals
study: Target triple, ABI, API level, libc and host tools
implementation: Create an Android CMake configuration for your educational engine; retain host tests
acceptance: The same source builds for host and arm64-v8a with separate build directories

subject: Deploy the tiny engine
study: Executable permissions, library paths and file locations
implementation: Push the native CLI and tiny checkpoint through ADB and run fixed token-ID input
acceptance: On-phone logits match the host within justified tolerance; distinguish ISA-related numeric differences from bugs

subject: Symbols and crashes
study: Debug symbols, backtraces and address-to-line mapping
implementation: Create an isolated debug crash and symbolize it; repair the bug
acceptance: The trace identifies your source function; do not distribute the intentional crash in the app

subject: Android logs and errors
study: logcat, native error propagation and app-visible diagnostics
implementation: Add structured stage logs without logging document contents by default
acceptance: A missing checkpoint and unsupported format generate useful diagnostics and a nonzero CLI status

subject: Native profiling
study: Simpleperf permissions, sample collection and symbol resolution
implementation: Profile a debuggable or otherwise supported native target; fall back to scoped timing if restricted
acceptance: State which counters and traces are actually available; never fabricate unavailable hardware measurements

subject: Memory accounting
study: RSS/PSS, file mappings, shared pages and allocator behavior
implementation: Collect available process memory information while loading, prefilling and decoding
acceptance: Explain why mapped bytes, RSS and PSS differ; preserve raw tool output alongside parsed values

subject: Device parity gate
study: Host-target reproducibility and compatibility
implementation: Write exact build, deploy and run instructions for the pinned versions
acceptance: Recreate the run from a clean shell; document ABI, Android version, model revision and backend

subject: Kotlin essentials
study: val/var, functions, classes, nullability and basic collections
implementation: Build a tiny Android screen displaying selected model metadata; avoid complex UI architecture
acceptance: Understand every Kotlin statement used; the app installs and runs without inference dependencies

subject: JNI boundary design
study: Opaque handles, ownership, native exceptions and API contracts
implementation: Specify create, load, generate, cancel, reset and destroy operations before implementing them
acceptance: Document valid call sequences and invalid handle behavior; no C++ exception crosses JNI unchecked

subject: Native library integration
study: Shared-library packaging, ABI selection and library loading
implementation: Load a native library and call a small metadata or dot-product function from Kotlin
acceptance: Verify the packaged ABI matches the phone; failure to load is visible and diagnosable

subject: Background execution
study: UI thread, worker ownership and nonblocking callbacks
implementation: Run a simulated token stream on a background worker and display updates
acceptance: UI remains responsive; callback ordering and worker lifetime are documented

subject: Real streaming inference
study: JNI string/array conversion, token bytes and buffering
implementation: Connect the runtime and stream generated text, preserving valid UTF-8 assembly
acceptance: A non-ASCII prompt and output do not corrupt text; first-token display timing is measured at the UI boundary

subject: Stop and cleanup
study: Cooperative stop, session state and resource release
implementation: Implement stop, reset and model release with explicit state transitions
acceptance: Rapid start/stop cannot use a freed handle; exactly one terminal status reaches the UI

subject: Application milestone
study: Minimal surface and observable behavior
implementation: Demonstrate prompt, streaming output, stop and metadata in airplane mode
acceptance: No network service is needed for inference after assets are installed; keep logs of a complete request lifecycle

subject: Activity recreation
study: UI state versus native engine ownership
implementation: Test rotation or recreation during generation; decide where the engine lifetime belongs
acceptance: No duplicate generation or orphaned callback; explain behavior instead of suppressing lifecycle events blindly

subject: Background and process loss
study: Background limits, process death and recoverable state
implementation: Define whether generation pauses, cancels or continues only under permitted app behavior; persist lightweight metadata
acceptance: Relaunch is coherent after process termination; do not promise survival without the required Android execution model

subject: Model switching
study: Unloading order, outstanding requests and memory peaks
implementation: Implement sequential model switching or simulate it if only one asset is available
acceptance: Reject or queue new requests during switch; no callback references unloaded state

subject: Sustained workload design
study: Thermal state, charging, ambient conditions and run order
implementation: Run a 10-15 minute sequence with repeated fixed requests; log throughput and thermal status when available
acceptance: Plot performance over time; report test conditions and any throttling indicators without inferring unsupported sensor values

subject: Energy measurement limits
study: Power versus energy, battery gauge noise and external meters
implementation: Define an energy experiment; use coarse battery deltas only as exploratory evidence if no reliable meter exists
acceptance: Do not claim precise joules per token from a brief percentage change; state measurement uncertainty

subject: Resource-budget policy
study: Queue size, context cap, token budget and memory-pressure response
implementation: Implement conservative limits and a clear out-of-budget message
acceptance: Over-limit requests fail before excessive allocation; document how limits were chosen from measurements

subject: Reliability gate
study: Repeated cancellation, load/unload and state transitions
implementation: Run a structured lifecycle soak test with failure injection and raw logs
acceptance: No uncontrolled memory growth in available measurements; list remaining platform restrictions

subject: Export concepts
study: Eager execution, captured graphs, shape constraints and graph breaks
implementation: Export a tiny linear model with torch.export and inspect the graph
acceptance: Explain parameters, inputs, outputs and shape guards; pin compatible package versions

subject: Small-model deployment
study: Portable runtime artifact and C++ runner
implementation: Follow a minimal ExecuTorch tutorial before an LLM example; deploy a tiny supported model
acceptance: Compare native outputs against Python; capture serialization and runtime versions

subject: Operator coverage
study: Supported ops, decomposition and backend requirements
implementation: Inspect an encoder or small transformer subgraph and list required operations
acceptance: Identify unsupported ops before lengthy conversion; distinguish export failure from execution failure

subject: Quantized export
study: Calibration, operator-level quantization and numerical checking
implementation: Quantize and export a small supported model following the selected backend recipe
acceptance: Record scale/dtype decisions and output drift; avoid assuming your educational INT4 is accepted

subject: Delegation and fallback
study: Partitioned graphs, data transfer and backend logs
implementation: Run a documented delegate example and inspect what was delegated
acceptance: Save evidence of actual backend execution; a successful API call alone is not proof of NPU use

subject: Documented LLM attempt
study: Known-supported model and end-to-end recipe
implementation: Attempt one pinned official LLM workflow with a predeclared time budget; preserve each failure stage
acceptance: If blocked, provide a minimal reproducible issue and retain the small-model success as the milestone

subject: Export milestone
study: Compatibility matrix and evidence
implementation: Write model, shape, dtype, target and delegated-op compatibility tables
acceptance: Separate verified support, documented-but-untested support and failed experiments

subject: Choose one vendor route
study: Genie versus ExecuTorch Qualcomm backend; SDK and target compatibility
implementation: Select one supported official example and record required SDK, device family and assets
acceptance: Confirm documentation applies to your target or state the gap; do not mix incompatible release instructions

subject: Prepare reproducible assets
study: Model revision, compiler options and target-specific artifacts
implementation: Obtain or compile supported model assets; hash every configuration and binary used
acceptance: A manifest links each artifact to its source and target; respect model terms and keep credentials out of records

subject: First target execution
study: Runtime libraries, initialization and diagnostic logs
implementation: Run the smallest supported example; capture complete initialization and execution logs
acceptance: Classify errors as asset, ABI, library, operator or device compatibility failures

subject: Numerical validation
study: Reference outputs and preprocessing equivalence
implementation: Compare vendor-run output with the appropriate reference using fixed token IDs or tensors
acceptance: Tokenizer and model configuration agree; task-level behavior meets a stated threshold

subject: Prefill and decode configuration
study: Supported sequence shapes, cache layout and preparation cost
implementation: Vary only documented options for one model; record first-use and repeated-run behavior
acceptance: Do not infer unrestricted dynamic shapes from one working sequence; list actual supported configurations

subject: Partitioning and overhead
study: Host work, accelerator work, transfers and synchronization
implementation: Inspect profiling or logs for fallback and transfer boundaries; estimate their contribution only where observable
acceptance: Separate measured timings from inferred bottlenecks; save raw traces

subject: Vendor path gate
study: Practical support and reproducibility
implementation: Write a setup guide or a high-quality failure report with a CPU fallback path
acceptance: The roadmap continues even if OEM firmware blocks NPU access; no root requirement is invented

subject: Upstream Snapdragon backend
study: CPU, Adreno and experimental Hexagon paths in the pinned runtime
implementation: Attempt the upstream Snapdragon path using its exact current instructions; enumerate actual devices
acceptance: Record what initializes and what runs; do not assume a GPU-looking offload flag proves GPU rather than another backend

subject: Comparison contract
study: Same-model comparisons versus whole-system comparisons
implementation: Define a matrix with runtime, quant, template, context, token counts and backend
acceptance: Mark unavoidable differences explicitly; avoid calling a different quantized model a hardware-only comparison

subject: Automated matrix
study: Configuration files, repetitions, timeout handling and result schema
implementation: Extend the Python runner to execute the small comparison matrix and resume incomplete experiments
acceptance: Failed runs remain visible and do not become zero latency; preserve raw logs

subject: Second application runtime
study: LiteRT-LM architecture and model packaging
implementation: Read its official integration path; optionally run one supported sample if time remains
acceptance: Document tested versus untested behavior; do not expand scope if core comparisons remain incomplete

subject: Request scheduling
study: Single-user latency, bounded queues and admission control
implementation: Add one-worker queueing to your native service or app and measure queue time separately
acceptance: Concurrent requests cannot corrupt session state; reject overload predictably

subject: Prefix reuse and cache validity
study: Exact token-prefix match, model identity and template identity
implementation: Implement a small cache-key experiment or simulation with explicit invalidation
acceptance: Changing model, template or token prefix prevents invalid reuse; measure benefit only for repeated prefixes

subject: Deployment decision
study: Latency, quality, memory, compatibility and sustained behavior
implementation: Choose a backend for the capstone using a decision table; include engineering complexity
acceptance: The choice follows your measurements; unsupported accelerators remain an optional branch

subject: Capstone scope
study: Offline requirements, public data, task definition and budgets
implementation: Choose a small public corpus and 20 initial questions; define target memory, latency and quality envelopes
acceptance: Budgets are provisional hypotheses; avoid importing sensitive work documents

subject: Text ingestion
study: Encoding, document identity, page/source metadata and incremental updates
implementation: Implement text or pre-extracted PDF text import with stable source IDs
acceptance: Every chunk can be traced to a source location; invalid text input gets an explicit result

subject: Chunking baseline
study: Boundaries, overlap, token budget and provenance
implementation: Implement deterministic chunking and fixtures for headings, short sections and long paragraphs
acceptance: No dropped or duplicated source spans beyond deliberate overlap; metadata survives splitting

subject: Embedding baseline
study: Normalization, similarity choice and model residency
implementation: Deploy a small supported embedding model or precompute embeddings on host for the first baseline
acceptance: Label precomputed versus fully on-device stages; compare identical text preprocessing

subject: Exact retrieval
study: Cosine or dot similarity, top-k, stable ties and index persistence
implementation: Implement exact vector search over the small corpus and a persisted index manifest
acceptance: Compare against a Python oracle; query and index embedding versions must match

subject: Answer assembly
study: Prompt budget, source labels, truncation and abstention
implementation: Build a retrieved-context prompt with a strict token budget and requested citations
acceptance: Long retrieval output cannot overflow the session; missing evidence yields an abstention path

subject: RAG baseline gate
study: Traceability and stage-level measurements
implementation: Run the first end-to-end questions offline and save retrieval plus answer traces
acceptance: Report retrieval, prompt construction, prefill and decode separately; inspect cited sources manually

subject: Residency policy
study: Embedding and generator memory, sequential loading and peak allocations
implementation: Compare keeping both models resident with loading one on demand
acceptance: Measure transition latency and available memory; choose a policy based on the phone rather than model file sizes

subject: Session budgeting
study: Context occupancy, source compression and history limits
implementation: Implement bounded history and explicit source selection; keep provenance after truncation
acceptance: No hidden loss of system instructions or source labels; test a full-context request

subject: Index update integrity
study: Versioning, crash recovery and atomic replacement
implementation: Build a new index separately, validate it, then activate it atomically where supported
acceptance: Interrupted updates leave the previous valid index usable; reject embedding-version mismatch

subject: Structured extraction task
study: Schema validation, evidence spans and unsupported claims
implementation: Add a narrow document extraction task such as dates and identifiers with citations
acceptance: Validate schema and source evidence; invalid output cannot silently become trusted data

subject: Optional audio or vision branch
study: Preprocessing, encoder cost, streaming and model scheduling
implementation: Choose one tiny supported speech or vision example; if core work is unfinished, use the session for debugging instead
acceptance: Measure preprocessing and inference separately; label this as optional and never block the text capstone

subject: Failure injection
study: Corrupt assets, cancellation, missing index and invalid configuration
implementation: Create a small failure matrix and exercise recovery paths in the app
acceptance: Each failure has a useful user-visible result and a diagnostic log without private content

subject: Resource-policy gate
study: Quality versus memory and latency
implementation: Write a policy note covering residency, budgets, queueing and model choice
acceptance: Explain the worst observed failure and what remains unmeasured; do not claim reliability from one happy-path demo

subject: Evaluation dataset
study: Answerable, unanswerable, cross-passage and distracting evidence cases
implementation: Expand to approximately 50 carefully reviewed questions with gold sources and scoring rubrics
acceptance: Separate tuning examples from a held-out subset; retain source version and author review status

subject: Retrieval evaluation
study: Recall at k, source relevance and failure categorization
implementation: Calculate retrieval metrics before generation; inspect misses by chunking and embedding cause
acceptance: Do not credit generation for evidence the retriever never supplied; report denominators

subject: Answer and citation scoring
study: Correctness, support, citation validity and appropriate abstention
implementation: Score answers with a human-readable rubric; use any model judge only as a secondary signal
acceptance: Manually audit disagreements and representative failures; distinguish correctness from fluent phrasing

subject: Performance evaluation
study: Stage timings, percentile estimates and sustained runs
implementation: Run the fixed set under controlled conditions and preserve per-request records
acceptance: Small samples are not sold as reliable tail percentiles; include individual failures and warmup policy

subject: Regression suite
study: Frozen fixtures, acceptable drift and compatibility gates
implementation: Create release checks for tokenization, numeric parity, schema output and lifecycle behavior
acceptance: A deliberately changed template or bad model manifest is detected; tolerances have a documented reason

subject: Ablation study
study: One variable at a time and interaction effects
implementation: Compare two context budgets or retrieval settings using the held-out protocol
acceptance: Report quality and latency together; avoid selecting a winner on the same examples used repeatedly for tuning

subject: Evaluation gate
study: Evidence-based claims and practical limits
implementation: Write a report with failures, sample sizes and the chosen operating point
acceptance: All tables can be regenerated from saved records; conclusions fit the measured scope

subject: Model packaging
study: Hashes, manifests, compatibility, licenses and asset versioning
implementation: Define a manifest and validate required files, runtime compatibility and hashes before activation
acceptance: A tampered asset is rejected; include model origin and required terms without redistributing restricted weights

subject: Interrupted installation
study: Temporary downloads/copies, validation and atomic activation
implementation: Implement interrupted asset-install recovery using small fixtures before large files
acceptance: The old valid model remains usable; incomplete assets are never selected as active

subject: Clean build and installation
study: Dependency pinning, reproducible instructions and device setup
implementation: Build from a clean directory and install using only documented steps
acceptance: Record any manual step you previously forgot; avoid claiming bit-for-bit reproducibility unless measured

subject: Soak and lifecycle release check
study: Repeated requests, cancellations, model switching and process restart
implementation: Run a bounded scripted reliability session and inspect memory plus errors
acceptance: Every failure is triaged; unresolved issues appear in known limitations rather than being hidden

subject: Portfolio documentation
study: Architecture, tradeoffs, measurements and readable code
implementation: Write three READMEs for the educational engine, benchmark suite and capstone; include one optimization case study
acceptance: Another engineer can find the important code and reproduce a result without chat history

subject: Upstream contribution preparation
study: Minimal reproduction, regression tests and project conventions
implementation: Prepare a small local patch, issue draft or documentation correction for a real observed problem
acceptance: No external message is sent automatically; your contribution is specific, reproducible and respectful of project scope

subject: Final reconstruction and next plan
study: Independent understanding and specialization choice
implementation: Explain the complete request path; reimplement one critical kernel from memory; choose ARM, NPU/compiler or runtime infrastructure for the next eight weeks
acceptance: Score the milestone rubric honestly; produce a concrete next-month plan based on the weakest demonstrated skill
